title: OpenZeppelin AccessControl DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE()
detects: A role-based admin system. The getter exists only on contracts that inherit AccessControl, where privileges are held per role rather than by a single owner.
knownFalseNegative: Before 0.2.0 this pattern called hasRole(bytes32,address) with no arguments, which always reverts, so it could never fire and every contract read as having no role system. The getter proves a role system exists; it cannot enumerate who holds which role, so a contract that renounced Ownable while keeping a MINTER_ROLE is reported as having admin authority without naming the holder. A role system whose every role has been renounced still answers this call.

coversExamples.observed: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE() returns 0x00..00, the role system is present
reverts, USDC does not use AccessControl

rationale: Role systems are how most tokens written since 2020 hold privileges, and they are invisible to owner()-only detection, which is how renounced ownership becomes theatre. Without a working read of this shape, a token administered through roles reports no admin at all.
